description: Find the value of one calculator input that makes an output equal a target — e.g. the trace width that gives 50 Ω on microstrip-impedance, or the gap that gives 90 Ω on differential-pair. The search runs server-side on rftools.io and costs one metered call: it needs an API key, the same one POST /calculate itself requires — unlike run_calculation, this does not run locally or for free. `reached: false` means no value in the search range reaches the target, and the value returned is the nearest one found instead. Use get_calculator_info first for the calculator's input and output keys and their stated bounds (min/max) — solveFor needs an explicit `range` when it states no bound.

grid.description: Round the solved value to the nearest multiple of this manufacturing grid, e.g. 0.001 (mm). Omit for the unrounded solution.

inputs.description: The calculator's other inputs, keyed by input name (the input named by solveFor is not one of these — e.g. {"substrateHeight": 1.6, "dielectricConstant": 4.2, "copperThickness": 35})

range.description: [low, high], narrowing the search inside solveFor's stated bound. Required when get_calculator_info shows no min/max for solveFor.

solveFor.description: Which declared numeric input to solve for (e.g. "traceWidth")

output.description: The output key to bring to a value (e.g. "impedance")

value.description: The value that output should equal

name: solve_calculation
title: Solve Calculation
